mean: success comes naturally when conditions are ripe
lit: when the water arrives, a channel forms by itself

story.text: Exiled to Huangzhou on a very small income, Su Shi wrote to his friend Qin Guan describing how he got by: he rationed his savings strictly, allowing himself a fixed small sum for each day. As for what he would do when the savings ran out, he said he would not plan it now: when the water comes, the channel forms by itself, so there was no need to worry in advance.

use.how: Predicate or attributive (水到渠成的事): says a result follows easily because the groundwork has already been laid. Describes an outcome, not an action someone performs.

near.diff: 顺理成章 says something follows logically or reasonably; 水到渠成 says a result arrives on its own once enough conditions have built up.

cue: A small bakery spent years perfecting its bread and winning loyal regulars; opening a second shop then happened with almost no strain. How do you describe it?

ctx.s: 只要你坚持练习，到时候自然{水到渠成}。
ctx.en: As long as you keep practising, it will all fall into place when the time comes.

ctx.s: 这支球队磨合了整整两个赛季，今年夺冠可以说是{水到渠成}。
ctx.en: The team spent two whole seasons gelling together, so winning the title this year came about quite naturally.

ctx.s: 先把基础打扎实，好成绩就会{水到渠成}。
ctx.en: Get the basics solid first, and good marks will follow naturally.

ctx.s: “合作什么时候能签下来？”“双方信任建立起来，签约自然{水到渠成}。”
ctx.en: "When will the partnership be signed?" "Once the two sides trust each other, the signing will follow naturally."

ctx.s: 别急着逼他表态，等时机成熟，一切都会{水到渠成}。
ctx.en: Don't push him to commit yet; when the time is right, everything will come together.

ctx.s: 他在这个领域默默积累了十年，去年出版专著可谓{水到渠成}。
ctx.en: He quietly built up ten years of work in the field, so publishing a monograph last year came quite naturally.

bad.s: 他运气真好，几乎没准备就{水到渠成}地拿了冠军。
bad.en: (meant: he was lucky and won without preparing)
bad.why: It describes success that follows from groundwork already laid, not luck without preparation.

bad.s: 我今晚一定要{水到渠成}这份报告。
bad.en: (meant: I must finish this report tonight)
bad.why: It is not a transitive verb for doing a task; it describes a result that comes about naturally.

mean: to prepare in advance before trouble comes
lit: before the rain comes, bind the nest tight

story.text: In an ancient poem a bird speaks: an owl has already carried off its young, and now, before the sky turns dark with rain, it gathers mulberry roots and binds up the openings of its nest so that it will hold. The image of securing the home before the rain became the idiom for preparing ahead of trouble.

use.how: Intransitive predicate, often after 要, 必须, 提前 or 这叫: 我们要未雨绸缪。 Praises or urges preparation made before a problem arrives.

near.diff: 亡羊补牢 is repairing things after a loss has happened; 未雨绸缪 is preparing before anything has gone wrong.

cue: Business is booming, yet the owner sets aside an emergency fund and trains backup staff in case hard times come. What is she doing?

ctx.s: 趁年轻多存点钱，就是在{未雨绸缪}。
ctx.en: Saving a bit more while you're young is a way of preparing for the future.

ctx.s: 公司趁业务好的时候{未雨绸缪}，提前培训后备人员。
ctx.en: While business is good, the company is preparing ahead by training backup staff early.

ctx.s: 台风季节快到了，市里已经开始{未雨绸缪}，清理排水管道。
ctx.en: Typhoon season is near, and the city has already started preparing by clearing the drains.

ctx.s: “现在生意这么好，为什么还要准备应急资金？”“就得趁现在{未雨绸缪}，不能等出了问题再想办法。”
ctx.en: "Business is so good right now, why set up an emergency fund?" "Now is exactly when to plan ahead; we can't wait until something goes wrong."

ctx.s: 面对人口老龄化，社会必须{未雨绸缪}，尽早完善养老体系。
ctx.en: Facing an ageing population, society must prepare ahead and improve the pension system early.

ctx.s: 她做事向来{未雨绸缪}，重要文件总要备份好几份。
ctx.en: She always plans ahead; she keeps several backups of every important file.

bad.s: 房子被淹了以后，我们才{未雨绸缪}，买了抽水机。
bad.en: (meant: after the flood we finally bought a pump)
bad.why: It means preparing before trouble arrives; buying the pump only after the flood is fixing things too late.

bad.s: 我们要{未雨绸缪}这次考试。
bad.en: (meant: we should prepare for this exam in advance)
bad.why: It takes no object; what you prepare for must come before it with a preposition meaning 'for', or use a plain verb meaning 'prepare'.

mean: to alert the target by acting too soon
lit: beat the grass and startle the snake hiding in it

use.how: Predicate, very often after 免得, 以免, 为了不 or 小心: 先别问他，免得打草惊蛇。 Warns against a premature move that tips off someone you are watching.

cue: You suspect a colleague is fiddling the accounts, but if you question him now he will simply destroy the evidence. Why do you wait?

ctx.s: 先别去问他，免得{打草惊蛇}。
ctx.en: Don't ask him yet, or you'll tip him off.

ctx.s: 警方掌握了线索，但为了不{打草惊蛇}，暂时没有行动。
ctx.en: The police have leads, but they are holding back for now so as not to alert the suspects.

ctx.s: 你现在就去质问他，不是{打草惊蛇}吗？
ctx.en: If you confront him now, won't that just warn him?

ctx.s: 想给她一个生日惊喜，就别到处打听，小心{打草惊蛇}。
ctx.en: If you want to surprise her on her birthday, stop asking around, or she'll catch on.

ctx.s: 调查人员悄悄收集证据，生怕{打草惊蛇}。
ctx.en: The investigators gathered evidence quietly, afraid of alerting their target.

ctx.s: 公司早就怀疑他泄露数据，可一次过早的谈话{打草惊蛇}，他第二天就辞职了。
ctx.en: The company had long suspected him of leaking data, but a premature talk tipped him off and he quit the next day.

bad.s: 他突然大叫一声，把孩子们{打草惊蛇}了。
bad.en: (meant: his sudden shout frightened the children)
bad.why: It does not mean to frighten someone; it means to warn a target you are pursuing by moving too early.

bad.s: 这次突击检查{打草惊蛇}，一下子就发现了很多问题。
bad.en: (meant: the surprise inspection shook things up and exposed problems)
bad.why: It names a mistake that lets the target escape, never an effective move that uncovers things.

mean: a lesson from someone else's mistake
lit: the overturned cart ahead serves as a mirror for those behind

story.text: The Han statesman Jia Yi, urging the emperor to reform, quoted a common saying: when the cart in front overturns, the cart behind takes warning. The Qin dynasty had collapsed so quickly, he argued, and if Han did not avoid the road Qin had taken, it would overturn in the same way.

use.how: A noun: 是……的前车之鉴, 有了……的前车之鉴, 以……为前车之鉴. Refers to someone's failure that serves as a warning to others.

near.diff: 前车之鉴 is the warning itself, a noun; 重蹈覆辙 is a verb for ignoring such a warning and repeating the mistake.

cue: Friends ask why you rent instead of buying a huge house on a big loan. You point to your brother, who did exactly that and struggled for years.

ctx.s: 他的失败就是我们的{前车之鉴}。
ctx.en: His failure is a warning to all of us.

ctx.s: 有了上次的{前车之鉴}，这回大家都提前订了票。
ctx.en: After what happened last time, everyone booked their tickets early this time.

ctx.s: 邻居被骗的事就是{前车之鉴}，陌生电话千万别轻信。
ctx.en: What happened to the neighbour who got scammed is a lesson: never trust calls from strangers.

ctx.s: “你为什么不贷款买大房子？”“我哥就是{前车之鉴}啊。”
ctx.en: "Why don't you take out a loan for a big house?" "Look at my brother, that's why."

ctx.s: 那家公司因盲目扩张而倒闭，应当成为同行的{前车之鉴}。
ctx.en: That company went bankrupt through reckless expansion, and it should serve as a warning to others in the industry.

ctx.s: 历史上的许多教训，都是后人的{前车之鉴}。
ctx.en: Many lessons of history are warnings for those who come after.

bad.s: 我{前车之鉴}了他的错误，所以没有犯同样的错。
bad.en: (meant: I learned from his mistake)
bad.why: It is a noun, not a verb: you take someone's mistake as one, you cannot do it to a mistake.

bad.s: 他成功创业的经验是我的{前车之鉴}。
bad.en: (meant: his success is a model for me)
bad.why: It is a warning drawn from someone's failure, never a successful example to copy.

lit: to tread again in the ruts of a cart that overturned

use.how: Intransitive predicate, often after 以免, 避免, 不要, 又 or 会: 以免重蹈覆辙。 Said of repeating a failure, one's own or someone else's, despite knowing better.

near.diff: 前车之鉴 is the warning a past failure gives; 重蹈覆辙 is failing to heed it and making the same mistake again.

cue: A firm nearly went bankrupt by expanding too fast. Ten years later its new boss starts opening branches everywhere in exactly the same way.

ctx.s: 吸取教训吧，千万别再{重蹈覆辙}。
ctx.en: Learn the lesson, and whatever you do, don't make the same mistake again.

ctx.s: 我们必须改进管理制度，以免{重蹈覆辙}。
ctx.en: We must improve our management system so we don't repeat the same failure.

ctx.s: 他明知上次投资失败的原因，这次却又{重蹈覆辙}。
ctx.en: He knew exactly why his last investment failed, yet this time he made the same mistake.

ctx.s: “这次还按老办法做吗？”“不行，那样只会{重蹈覆辙}。”
ctx.en: "Shall we do it the old way again?" "No, that would only repeat the same failure."

ctx.s: 不少企业没有吸取前人的教训，最终{重蹈覆辙}。
ctx.en: Many companies failed to learn from those before them and ended up going the same way.

ctx.s: 这部纪录片提醒观众，忘记历史就可能{重蹈覆辙}。
ctx.en: The documentary reminds viewers that forgetting history can mean repeating its mistakes.

bad.s: 她每天都{重蹈覆辙}，走同一条路去上班。
bad.en: (meant: she takes the same route to work every day)
bad.why: It means repeating a mistake or failure, not simply doing the same thing as a routine.

bad.s: 老师让我把这道题{重蹈覆辙}一遍。
bad.en: (meant: the teacher made me redo this problem)
bad.why: It takes no object and is not 'to redo'; it criticises repeating a past failure.

lit: too late even to decide where to put one's hands

use.how: Predicate after 让/令 or 一时, or in 打了……一个措手不及. Said when something sudden leaves no time to respond.

near.diff: 惊慌失措 stresses panic and losing one's head; 措手不及 stresses having no time to respond to something sudden.

cue: In the last five minutes the other team suddenly switched tactics, and your side had no time at all to respond.

ctx.s: 突如其来的大雨让我们{措手不及}。
ctx.en: The sudden downpour caught us completely off guard.

ctx.s: 对方在最后几分钟突然改变战术，打了我们一个{措手不及}。
ctx.en: In the last few minutes they suddenly changed tactics and caught us flat-footed.

ctx.s: 面试官的问题出乎意料，他一时{措手不及}，没来得及想好怎么回答。
ctx.en: The interviewer's question was so unexpected that he was caught off guard and had no time to work out an answer.

ctx.s: “怎么连备用方案都没有？”“谁想到系统会突然崩溃，大家都{措手不及}啊。”
ctx.en: "How come there wasn't even a backup plan?" "Who knew the system would crash out of nowhere? Everyone was caught off guard."

ctx.s: 收购价格突然大幅下跌，许多农民{措手不及}，损失惨重。
ctx.en: The purchase price suddenly plunged, catching many farmers unprepared and causing heavy losses.

ctx.s: 提前做好准备，变化来临时才不会{措手不及}。
ctx.en: Prepare in advance, and you won't be caught off guard when change comes.

bad.s: 他做事总是{措手不及}，经常丢三落四。
bad.en: (meant: he is clumsy and careless)
bad.why: It describes being caught by a sudden event, not a careless or clumsy personality.

bad.s: 我们三个月前就知道这件事了，所以大家都{措手不及}。
bad.en: (meant: we knew three months ago, so everyone was ready)
bad.why: It requires suddenness; with months of warning nobody is caught off guard, so the sentence contradicts itself.

mean: producing the opposite of the intended result

use.how: Predicate, often after 会, 可能, 往往 or 结果: 批评太多会适得其反。 Said of an action or method whose effect is the opposite of what it aimed at.

near.diff: 事与愿违 is any outcome contrary to one's hopes, often from outside causes; 适得其反 says one's own action caused the opposite effect.
弄巧成拙 stresses trying to be clever and spoiling things; 适得其反 is any measure that backfires, clever or not.

cue: A parent nags a teenager to study every single night, and soon the teenager refuses to open a book at all.

ctx.s: 对孩子批评太多，往往会{适得其反}。
ctx.en: Criticising children too much often backfires.

ctx.s: 减肥时一直饿肚子可能{适得其反}，让人更想吃东西。
ctx.en: Starving yourself on a diet can backfire and make you crave food even more.

ctx.s: 他想安慰她，一个劲儿地劝她别哭，结果{适得其反}，她哭得更厉害了。
ctx.en: He wanted to comfort her and kept telling her not to cry, but it had the opposite effect: she cried even harder.

ctx.s: “我天天催他复习，有用吗？”“催得太紧可能{适得其反}。”
ctx.en: "I nag him to revise every day. Does it help?" "Pushing too hard can backfire."

ctx.s: 过度包装本想吸引顾客，却{适得其反}，让人觉得产品不实在。
ctx.en: The lavish packaging was meant to attract customers, but it backfired and made the product seem insubstantial.

ctx.s: 专家提醒，滥用抗生素不但治不好病，还可能{适得其反}。
ctx.en: Experts warn that misusing antibiotics not only fails to cure illness but can make things worse.

bad.s: 他本来想去北京，可是航班取消了，真是{适得其反}。
bad.en: (meant: he wanted to go to Beijing but the flight was cancelled)
bad.why: Nothing he did backfired; an outside event simply spoiled his plan, so the idiom for things going against one's wishes fits instead.

bad.s: 这个方法很{适得其反}，大家都喜欢用。
bad.en: (meant: this method is very suitable)
bad.why: The first character does not mean 'suitable' here; the idiom means backfiring, and it cannot be modified by 'very'.

mean: things turn out contrary to one's wishes
lit: events and wishes go against each other

use.how: A clause on its own, usually after 可惜, 可是, 然而 or 结果: 可惜事与愿违。 Expresses regret that the outcome differed from what was hoped.

near.diff: 适得其反 says one's own action produced the opposite effect; 事与愿违 only says the outcome differed from the hope, whatever the cause.

cue: You had planned a quiet weekend at home, but your boss called and asked you to work both days. How do you sigh about it?

ctx.s: 我想周末好好休息，可惜{事与愿违}，又要加班。
ctx.en: I wanted a good rest at the weekend, but it wasn't to be: I have to work overtime again.

ctx.s: 他们本来打算在海边办婚礼，结果{事与愿违}，连下了一周雨。
ctx.en: They had planned a beach wedding, but things didn't go their way: it rained for a whole week.

ctx.s: 虽然大家都尽了力，但{事与愿违}，球队还是输了。
ctx.en: Everyone gave their all, but it didn't work out, and the team still lost.

ctx.s: “你不是要出国读书吗？”“是啊，可{事与愿违}，签证没批下来。”
ctx.en: "Weren't you going abroad to study?" "Yes, but it didn't work out. My visa was refused."

ctx.s: 人生常常{事与愿违}，重要的是怎样面对。
ctx.en: Life often doesn't go the way we want; what matters is how we face it.

ctx.s: 他希望退休后去各地旅行，然而{事与愿违}，身体一直不好。
ctx.en: He hoped to travel after retiring, but things turned out otherwise: his health has been poor ever since.

bad.s: 这次考试很顺利，一切都{事与愿违}。
bad.en: (meant: everything went as I wished)
bad.why: It means things went against one's wishes, so it cannot describe things going exactly as hoped.

bad.s: 这场大雨{事与愿违}了我们的计划。
bad.en: (meant: the rain ruined our plans)
bad.why: It is a self-contained clause and takes no object; the rain cannot do it to the plans. Use a verb such as 'disrupt' instead.

mean: too far behind ever to catch up
lit: to see only the dust of the one ahead and be unable to reach them

story.text: The Eastern Han official Zhao Zi, on his way to a new post, passed through Xingyang. The local magistrate, a man Zhao had once recommended for office, came out to the road to pay his respects, but Zhao did not stop. The magistrate followed him as far as the post station, yet could only gaze at the dust of his carriage without catching up.

use.how: Predicate, often after 让/令, 只能 or 真是: 他的水平我望尘莫及。 Admires someone far ahead; the subject or speaker is the one left behind.

cue: Your colleague speaks five languages fluently, while you are still struggling with your first. You say how far behind her you are.

ctx.s: 他的中文水平，我真是{望尘莫及}。
ctx.en: His Chinese is so good that I can't even come close.

ctx.s: 这家公司的技术实力让竞争对手{望尘莫及}。
ctx.en: This company's technical strength leaves its competitors far behind.

ctx.s: “你也能像她那样一天读完一本书吗？”“我哪儿行，只能{望尘莫及}。”
ctx.en: "Can you read a whole book in a day like her?" "Me? No way. I can only admire her from far behind."

ctx.s: 老王退休后开始跑马拉松，连年轻人都{望尘莫及}。
ctx.en: Old Wang took up marathons after retiring, and even young people can't keep up with him.

ctx.s: 论经验，我们这些新人对张师傅只能{望尘莫及}。
ctx.en: When it comes to experience, we newcomers are nowhere near Master Zhang.

ctx.s: 该市近年的发展速度，令周边地区{望尘莫及}。
ctx.en: The city's pace of development in recent years has left the surrounding regions far behind.

bad.s: 他的成绩比我差远了，我对他{望尘莫及}。
bad.en: (meant: he is far behind me)
bad.why: It is said by or about the one left behind; here the speaker is ahead, so the roles are reversed.

bad.s: 这道数学题太难了，我{望尘莫及}。
bad.en: (meant: this problem is beyond me)
bad.why: It compares you with a person far ahead of you, not with a task that is too hard for you.

mean: longing for one's child to become a great success
lit: to hope that one's son becomes a dragon

use.how: Predicate or attributive (望子成龙的父母), said only of parents and their own children; often comes with a hint of pressure. For daughters there is also 望女成凤.

cue: A mother signs her seven-year-old son up for piano, maths and English classes, dreaming that he will one day be a famous surgeon.

ctx.s: 天下父母都{望子成龙}。
ctx.en: All parents dream of their children doing great things.

ctx.s: 他父母{望子成龙}，从小就给他报了很多辅导班。
ctx.en: His parents had great hopes for him and signed him up for lots of tutoring classes from an early age.

ctx.s: {望子成龙}的心情可以理解，但不能给孩子太大压力。
ctx.en: Wanting your child to succeed is understandable, but you shouldn't put them under too much pressure.

ctx.s: “你为什么非要孩子学钢琴？”“当妈的谁不{望子成龙}呢？”
ctx.en: "Why do you insist your kid learns the piano?" "What mother doesn't want her child to shine?"

ctx.s: 在一些家庭里，{望子成龙}变成了沉重的负担。
ctx.en: In some families, parents' high hopes for their children have become a heavy burden.

ctx.s: 这部电视剧讲的是一位{望子成龙}的母亲和叛逆儿子的故事。
ctx.en: The TV series tells the story of a mother with sky-high hopes for her son and her rebellious boy.

bad.s: 我{望子成龙}，希望自己将来当上总经理。
bad.en: (meant: I hope to become general manager one day)
bad.why: It is a parent's hope for their child, never a person's ambition for themselves.

bad.s: 老板{望子成龙}，希望新员工快点成长起来。
bad.en: (meant: the boss hopes the new staff grow quickly)
bad.why: It is only used of parents and their own children, never of a boss and employees.
